assessmentNotes: Includes 2025/2026 Earth System assessment marking ocean acidification as the seventh transgressed boundary alongside climate, biosphere, land, freshwater, biogeochemical, and novel entities.

boundaries.name: Climate Change (Atmospheric CO2)
boundaries.source: NOAA Global Monitoring Laboratory / Mauna Loa
boundaries.description: Safe limit is 350 ppm. Current value has surpassed safe and is well inside the zone of high danger.

boundaries.name: Climate Change (Radiative Forcing)
boundaries.subsystem: Top of atmosphere net energy imbalance
boundaries.description: Radiative forcing exceeds 2.9 W/m² relative to pre-industrial, driving accelerated heating.

boundaries.name: Biosphere Integrity (Genetic Diversity)
boundaries.source: IUCN Red List / IPBES Global Assessment
boundaries.description: Extinctions are estimated at 10-100x natural background rate of 1 E/MSY.

boundaries.name: Biosphere Integrity (Functional Diversity)
boundaries.source: Natural History Museum BII / Scholes & Biggs
boundaries.description: Safe threshold is 90% intactness. Global average has fallen to ~76.5%.

boundaries.name: Land-System Change
boundaries.subsystem: Global biome intactness and forest cover
boundaries.source: FAO Global Forest Resources Assessment / Global Forest Watch
boundaries.description: Requires at least 75% forest biome intactness; estimated currently at ~60%.

boundaries.name: Freshwater Change (Blue Water)
boundaries.source: Gleick / Wada et al. / Richardson et al. (2023)
boundaries.description: Global blue water consumption exceeds safe boundary of 4,000 km³/yr with intense regional depletion.

boundaries.name: Freshwater Change (Green Water)
boundaries.controlVariable: Land area with root-zone soil moisture anomalies
boundaries.source: Wang-Erlandsson et al. (2022) / Richardson et al. (2023)
boundaries.description: Soil moisture disturbances exceed safe baseline over 18% of global land.

boundaries.name: Biogeochemical Flows (Nitrogen)
boundaries.subsystem: Industrial and intentional biological N fixation
boundaries.description: Over 3x higher than safe planetary boundary of 62 Tg N/yr.

boundaries.name: Biogeochemical Flows (Phosphorus)
boundaries.subsystem: Phosphorus mined and transferred into aquatic systems
boundaries.controlVariable: Phosphorus flow to freshwater and oceans
boundaries.source: Carpenter et al. / Richardson et al. (2023)
boundaries.description: Severe nutrient overloading in lakes and marine coastal zones.

boundaries.name: Ocean Acidification
boundaries.controlVariable: Global average surface seawater aragonite saturation (Ωarag)
boundaries.source: Potsdam Institute / Feely et al. / Copernicus Marine Service (2025/2026)
boundaries.description: Safe operating space boundary is set at >= 80% of pre-industrial aragonite saturation (2.75-2.80). Recent 2025/2026 assessments reveal widespread polar undersaturation and global mean crossing into high-risk zone.

boundaries.name: Atmospheric Aerosol Loading
boundaries.subsystem: Monsoons, albedo, and public health particulate burden
boundaries.description: Global mean is currently within the safe zone, but with acute regional hotspots across South and East Asia.

boundaries.name: Stratospheric Ozone Depletion
boundaries.source: WMO / UNEP Scientific Assessment of Ozone Depletion
boundaries.description: Successful international treaty (Montreal Protocol) has maintained ozone within the safe boundary, on track to complete global recovery by 2045-2066.

boundaries.name: Novel Entities (Pollution, Synthetics, E-Waste)
boundaries.subsystem: Chemical, plastic, microplastic, and e-waste toxics
boundaries.controlVariable: Composite chemical, PFAS, and electronic toxicity pressure index
boundaries.source: Persson et al. (2022) / UN E-Waste Monitor / Guliyeva et al. (2025)
boundaries.description: Hundreds of thousands of synthetic substances released at rates far exceeding global safety assessment and recycling capacities.
